summary: 1. High-stayed hooks open with an aggressive paradox, myth-debunk, or alarming punchline within the first 6 words rather than setting up a scenario. 2. Winning titles use active, visceral verbs and strong visual metaphors (e.g., 'Pineapples Eat You Back') rather than passive passive explanations. 3. Topic focus must center on personal body quirks or extreme sensory oddities rather than industrial objects or passive food production steps. 4. Videos under 25 seconds with 55%+ stayed rate outperform longer videos because they maintain concise pacing without filler setup sentences. 5. Opening lines containing rhetorical questions or slow storytelling ('Your car swerves...', 'Ever noticed...') trigger immediate swipes.
winning_hooks: Direct Myth Contradiction: State the common belief and immediately shatter it (e.g., 'Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.')
Visceral Threat / Personification: Frame everyday items aggressively (e.g., 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.')
Shocking Historical Anchor: Use extreme comparisons instead of exact measurements (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States.')
avoid: Preamble storytelling and scenario setups (e.g., 'Your car swerves off the highway...', 'Drop an apple or pear...')
Generic rhetorical opening questions (e.g., 'Ever noticed those tiny black dots...')
Dry textbook facts and definitions without emotional stakes (e.g., 'Honey is famous for being one of the only natural foods...')
Long, wordy explanatory hooks with scientific clauses (e.g., 'Garlic usually doesn't make you cry... because its defense chemicals work differently...')
next_experiment: Test Hook Frame A (Direct Paradox/Threat: 'Your stomach acid can dissolve steel, but it doesn't destroy you') vs Hook Frame B (Scenario Setup: 'Inside your body right now is an acid strong enough to melt metal') keeping video visual and title identical.
